OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
For integer $n\geq 1$ we define the factor difference set of $n$ by\[D(n) = \{\lvert a-b\rvert : n=ab\}.\]Is it true that, for every $k\geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1<\cdots<N_k$ such that\[\lvert \cap_i D(N_i)\rvert \geq k?\]
#885: [ErRo97]
number theory | 
divisors
A question of Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97], who proved this is true for $k=2$. Jiménez-Urroz [Ji99] proved this for $k=3$ and Bremner [Br19] proved this for $k=4$.

 Hello, I’ve been playing with Erdős Problem #885 in my spare time because I found it fun, and I wanted to share two partial results that seemed worth recording.
Disclosure: I used AI-assisted search, reformulation, computation, and pattern testing during exploration. I then consolidated the useful parts, formalized the posted statements in Lean with Aristotle, and checked the claims myself. I am not claiming a solution to #885; I am only posting two partial findings that, to the best of my literature search, I have not found recorded in the published #885 literature or on the Erdős Problems forum.
Repo: https://github.com/SamMausberg/lean-formalizations/tree/main/FormalConjectures/Problems/Erdos/E885/ForumNote
PDF: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EkIEg14iQezGVNVBXSEfm7Q8ar3af2Jk/view?usp=sharing
I am not claiming a solution of E885 itself, only these two formalized partial results.
As suggested, I wanted to put the claims from the PDF in this comment.The note contains two separate claims:
First, if\[
Y(a,b,c)=\{\, z>0 : z^2+a,\ z^2+b,\ z^2+c \text{ are all squares} \,\},
\]then\[
\{330,870,2445,4155,10482\}\subseteq Y(756000,15971200,45130176),
\]so\[
\bigl|Y(756000,15971200,45130176)\bigr| \ge 5.
\]In particular, the universal anchored bound\[
|Y(a,b,c)| \le 4
\]is false.
Second, and more directly in the language of E885, I prove the exact finite computation\[
D(79200)\cap D(227205)\cap D(1258560)=\{36,468,692,1028\}.
\]
 sammausberg
